role: L5 independent skeptic / A7 prereviewer of integrated pre-GO artifacts (audit only, no repair)
known_limitations: Audit depth: 54 of 1,200 census rows spot-checked in full (12 symbols, all 6 verdict classes) plus mechanical whole-file checks (counts, caps, lattice, exemplars, ancestry-id resolution for all 218 distinct tokens, parts-vs-merged diffs on 3 symbols) — not a row-by-row re-adjudication of all 1,200 verdicts; lane-level verdict judgment inside un-sampled rows is unverifiable at this depth.
Mechanism-class dup judgments (F-2 donchian asymmetry) are adjudicated on the written rule text and recorded ancestry only; no independent mechanism taxonomy was constructed.

Publication-clock facts for EFFR (08:00 vs 09:00 vs 09:30 ET) were NOT re-fetched from the network (charter law 1); the audit treats both in-file statements as morning-publication and checks the T-1 rule's safety under any of them (F-10).
NY-Fed/CBOE/EIA publication schedules were audited as design logic against the program's own PIT_SOURCE_TABLE statements, not against live network re-measurement.
No backtest, no scoring, no S1 access, no registry/ledger/MAP/LESSONS writes; no repairs made to any audited artifact (independence preserved — findings only).

merge_census.py priority-rubric deviation (F-3) was established by code reading + cap recomputation; subscores M/F/C are not stored per-row in the TSV, so per-row score reconstruction beyond caps/lattice was not possible.
